Word trends over time

Source: R/trends.R
word_trends.Rd

For each year (or group of years), reports the share of abstracts that mention a word. Words are cleaned the same way as in [topic_model()], so "student" also counts "students". Use it to see whether a concept is rising or fading across the literature.

Usage

word_trends(
  data,
  words = NULL,
  n = 8,
  year = "year",
  text = "abstract",
  bin = 1,
  stopwords = NULL,
  min_word_length = 3,
  singularize = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per reference.

words

Words to track, such as `c("equity", "belonging")`. If `NULL`, the `n` words found in the most abstracts overall are used.

n

Number of words to track when `words` is `NULL`.

year

Name of the column holding the publication year. Text such as "2019" or "Spring 2019" is fine; the first 4-digit number is used.

text

Name of the column holding the text to analyse.

bin

Width of each period in years (1 = one row per year).

stopwords

Extra words to drop, in addition to [citelens_stopwords()].

min_word_length

Drop words shorter than this many letters.

singularize

Merge simple plurals (default `TRUE`).

Value

A data frame with `period` (first year of the period), `term`, `n_docs` (abstracts mentioning it), `n_period` (abstracts in the period) and `share` (`n_docs / n_period`). Periods with no abstracts are omitted.

Details

Years with only a few abstracts give jumpy shares, so check `n_period` (the number of abstracts in that year) before reading much into a change. Use `bin` to group years, for example `bin = 5`.

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "sample_abstracts.bib", package = "citelens")
refs <- bib_to_df(f)
word_trends(refs, words = c("retention", "tuition"), bin = 5)
#>   period      term n_docs n_period     share
#> 1   2015 retention      7       18 0.3888889
#> 2   2020 retention      4       12 0.3333333
#> 3   2015   tuition      4       18 0.2222222
#> 4   2020   tuition      4       12 0.3333333
